content: The Roque Sáenz Peña Hospital, officially known in Spanish as Hospital Dr. Roque Sáenz Peña, is a public municipal healthcare facility located in Rosario, within the province of Santa Fe, Argentina. It functions as a secondary referral hospital, primarily serving the South and Southwest Districts of the city. The hospital is organized into three primary areas of care: 1. Children's Health Area: This division includes pediatrics, neonatology, and a pediatric emergency room. 2. Adults' Area: This section encompasses various medical specialties and a general emergency room. 3. Women's Area: This area features a birthing center, gynecology services, and an emergency room dedicated to obstetrics and gynecology. The labor ward at the hospital facilitates approximately 1,800 births annually. This department also runs a breastfeeding promotion program, which earned the hospital the designation of Mother and Child-Friendly Hospital (Hospital Amigo de la Madre y el Niño) from UNICEF Argentina. History The decision to establish a healthcare and first aid facility in the southern part of Rosario was made in 1921. The center officially opened on August 20, 1923, at its current location. In 1933, it was named after former Argentine President Roque Sáenz Peña. In 1961, a labor ward that had been operating in a separate building was integrated into the hospital.
